old_caption: The video depicts a classroom setting where an individual, dressed in a light blue shirt, dark tie, and black pants, stands in front of a whiteboard. The whiteboard displays a mathematical equation: "T = 2π√(m/k)." The person gestures towards the board while speaking, indicating an explanation or teaching moment. On the far right side of the frame, a black countertop with some small objects on it is visible. The background includes a plain wall with a small door or panel near the top right corner. The scene remains static throughout the video, focusing on the individual's interaction with the whiteboard and the equation presented.

caption: The video depicts a classroom scene where a man in a light shirt and patterned tie stands at the left, facing a whiteboard bearing the handwritten equation T = 2π√(m/k). His raised right arm continually repositions as he gestures, the open palm hovering near the equation on the left of the board. As the clip proceeds, that arm extends further right, the hand becoming an index-finger point aimed toward the suspended paper tape near the board's center. His torso and head turn slightly, revealing more of his face in profile, while his lowered left arm shifts a little with his body. A metal support frame at the right holds a vertical ruler and a weighted tape, with another weighted rod at the board's edge. These suspended elements and the brass weights on the table at the lower right remain fixed throughout.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.

"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
